fresh_external_evidence.delta: A fencing token is generation-scoped evidence passed to an external resource so stale owners can be rejected; current lock observation alone is not sufficient stale-owner safety.
Idempotency addresses duplicate retries; it does not replace caller/execution ownership fencing, and indeterminate provider outcomes remain a reconciliation concern.

forked descendants inherit file descriptors/open-file descriptions; flock state is associated with the open file description and can therefore survive into a child until all duplicated descriptors are closed or unlocked.
Python provides an after_in_child hook suitable for clearing/reseeding process-local capability registries if fork descendants must not inherit authority.

hypothesis: PR204's B1/B2/B3 structure is directionally correct, but exact-generation safety requires capability issuance and lifecycle semantics to survive ordinary cardinality, same-epoch logical execution identity, constructor forgery, fork/subprocess inheritance and provider-commit TOCTOU discriminators.
strongest_counterhypothesis: The current DB V15/V16 checks plus the physical FrankExecutionGate may still prevent a real provider effect from a forked or forged caller even where the transient capability model is imperfect; therefore the new fork result is a provenance/liveness falsifier, not evidence of an unauthenticated provider bypass.

normal_discriminating_test.name: SAME_EXECUTION_MULTI_EFFECT_CARDINALITY

observation.schema_fact: effect_id is PRIMARY KEY and binding_hash is globally UNIQUE
observation.runtime_fact: derive_execution_generation_fence reuses one secret for the same live FrankExecutionLease and therefore returns the same public binding/fingerprint/binding_hash for all effects under that execution

normal_discriminating_test.repair_candidate: Keep effect_id as the uniqueness key; either remove global UNIQUE from the generation identity hash or store a per-effect binding digest that includes effect_id while separately retaining a comparable generation identity.

out_of_box_experiment.name: FORKED_CAPABILITY_GHOST
out_of_box_experiment.question: Does PR204's process-local WeakKeyDictionary secret necessarily die when the source process retires, or can fork create an independently surviving child copy?
out_of_box_experiment.method: Minimal Linux/Python reproduction of WeakKeyDictionary[lease, secret], owner._closed, weak owner reference and capability fingerprint; derive in parent, fork, retire/remove parent copy, synchronize child, then call child-side liveness assertion.
out_of_box_experiment.interpretation: The process-local-secret design does not automatically die across fork because child memory and lock/open-file-description state may be inherited. This does not establish provider bypass; it establishes a missing fork/subprocess capability-lineage policy and regression obligation.
repair_candidates: If descendants must not inherit authority, clear/reseed capability issuance/liveness registries with os.register_at_fork(after_in_child=...) and add a fork discriminator.
If descendants are intentionally part of one admitted execution generation, model and test that lineage explicitly rather than relying on accidental inheritance.

existing_adversarial_findings_reused_not: PR204 B0: public FrankExecutionLease constructor permits live-looking same-field object forgery unless exact Gate issuance is registered and checked; PR217 addresses this lane.
PR204 exact V16 generation identity: fence does not bind execution_id/credential admission; PR211 tests same-epoch execution_id rebinding.
